arxiv-2211-01321.title: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI DI PADOVA
arxiv-2211-01321.creator: Dipartimento di Fisica e Astronomia “Galileo Galilei”
arxiv-2211-01321.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dipartimento di Fisica e Astronomia “Galileo Galilei”. Thesis supervisor

Candidate

Prof. Pierpaolo Mastrolia

Giacomo Brunello

Thesis co-supervisor

Dr. Mandal

Academic Year 2021/2022

Abstract

The discovery of gravitational waves (GWs) emitted by a binary coalescing system has oriented the scientific community towards the development and the application of advanced techniques to reveal gravitational waves and to study waveforms, in order to capture the main characteristics of the astrophysical objects that generate them and to discover new features of the gravitational interaction.

arxiv-2404-03341.title: Defect of irreducible plane curves with simple singularities
arxiv-2404-03341.creator: Piotr Pokora
arxiv-2404-03341.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Piotr Pokora. In this note we focus on the defect of singular plane curve that was recently introduced by Dimca. Roughly speaking, the defect of a reduced plane curve measures the discrepancy from the property of being a free curve. We find some lower-bound on the defect for certain classes of irreducible plane curves admitting nodes, ordinary cusps and ordinary triple points. The main result of the note tells us that reduced simply singular plane curves with sufficiently high Arnold exponents are never free.

arxiv-2405-04110.title: A Self-regulated Stochastic Acceleration Model of Pulsar Wind Nebulae
arxiv-2405-04110.creator: Shuta J. Tanaka, Wataru Ishizaki
arxiv-2405-04110.description: Abstract Pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) are clouds of the magnetized relativistic electron/positron plasma supplied from the central pulsar. However, the number of radio-emitting particles inside a PWN is larger than the expectation from the study of pulsar magnetospheres and then their origin is still unclear.

arxiv-2405-15798.title: Holographic dark energy with Granda-Oliveros cutoff and ansatz based approach : An extended look
arxiv-2405-15798.creator: Oem Trivedi, Maxim Khlopov
arxiv-2405-15798.description: Abstract Holographic dark energy models have proven to be a very interesting way to study various aspects of late-time acceleration of the universe. In this work we extensively study HDE models with the Granda-Oliveros cutoff with an ansatz based approach.

arxiv-2502-07153.title: Feature Importance Depends on Properties of the Data: Towards Choosing the Correct Explanations for Your Data and Decision Trees based Models
arxiv-2502-07153.creator: Célia Wafa AYAD, Thomas Bonnier, Benjamin Bosch, Sonali Parbhoo, Jesse Read
arxiv-2502-07153.description: Abstract In order to ensure the reliability of the explanations of machine learning models, it is crucial to establish their advantages and limits and in which case each of these methods outperform. However, the current understanding of when and how each method of explanation can be used is insufficient.

arxiv-2506-10328.title: Towards Scalable SOAP Note Generation: A Weakly Supervised Multimodal Framework
arxiv-2506-10328.creator: Sadia Kamal, Tim Oates, Joy Wan
arxiv-2506-10328.description: Abstract Skin carcinoma is the most prevalent form of cancer globally, accounting for over $8 billion in annual healthcare expenditures. In clinical settings, physicians document patient visits using detailed SOAP (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan) notes. However, manually generating these notes is labor-intensive and contributes to clinician burnout.

arxiv-2605-00022.title: Putting HUMANS first: Efficient LAM Evaluation with Human Preference Alignment
arxiv-2605-00022.creator: Woody Haosheng Gan, William Held, Diyi Yang

britannica-1911-anu.title: Anu (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-anu.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-anu.description: Article 'Anu' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. In the astral theology of Babylonia and Assyria, Anu, Bel and Ea became the three zones of the ecliptic, the northern, middle and southern zone respectively. The purely theoretical character of Anu is thus still further emphasized, and in the annals and votive inscriptions as well as in the incantations and hymns, he is rarely introduced as an active force to whom a personal appeal can be made.

hunter-venereal-disease-1786.title: A Treatise on the Venereal Disease
hunter-venereal-disease-1786.creator: John Hunter
hunter-venereal-disease-1786.description: Hunter's 1786 treatise on venereal disease — the first systematic clinical and experimental study of syphilis and gonorrhoea, including his famous (and self-disastrous) self-inoculation experiment. First edition.

petrie-ten-years-digging-1892.title: Ten Years' Digging in Egypt, 1881-1891
petrie-ten-years-digging-1892.creator: W. M. Flinders Petrie
petrie-ten-years-digging-1892.description: Petrie's own summary of the decade that invented scientific archaeology — stratigraphy, sequence dating, and the method everything since builds on.

pmc-10568697.title: Improving the Dust Removal Efficiency of a Natural Gas Filter: An Experimental and Numerical Simulation Study
pmc-10568697.creator: Sijia Zheng, Zhixiang Dai, Feng Wang, Qin Bie, Xinyi Wang, Xubing Liu, Lin Zhong
pmc-10568697.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study aims to evaluate the dust removal efficiency and working conditions of a filter separator through a pressure drop under various operating conditions. Typical horizontal filter separators in natural gas stations were taken as the research objects, and the computational fluid dynamics method was first attempted to investigate the static and dynamic characteristics of the pressure drop and the dust removal efficiency under different operating times and pressures. Then, the simulated results were compared with those obtained from online dust detection.

pmc-10643163.title: Transcriptome and coexpression network analysis reveals properties and candidate genes associated with grape (Vitis vinifera L.) heat tolerance
pmc-10643163.creator: Jiuyun Wu, Fuchun Zhang, Guohong Liu, Riziwangguli Abudureheman, Shijian Bai, Xinyu Wu, Chuan Zhang, Yaning Ma, Xiping Wang, Qian Zha, Haixia Zhong
pmc-10643163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Temperature is one of the most important environmental factors affecting grape season growth and geographical distribution. With global warming and the increasing occurrence of extreme high-temperature weather, the impact of high temperatures on grape production has intensified. Therefore, identifying the molecular regulatory networks and key genes involved in grape heat tolerance is crucial for improving the resistance of grapes and promoting sustainable development in grape production.

pmc-10675139.title: Enhanced Low-Density Silicone Foams Blown by Water–Hydroxyl Blends
pmc-10675139.creator: Ingrid Rebane, Karl Jakob Levin, Uno Mäeorg, Urmas Johanson, Peeter Piirimägi, Tauri Tätte, Tarmo Tamm
pmc-10675139.description: Water, alcohols, diols, and glycerol are low-cost blowing agents that can be used to create the desired silicone foam structures. Although their combined use can be beneficial, it remains unclear how it affects the physical properties of the resulting materials.

pmc-11311900.title: From chaos to kaleidoscope: Exploring factors in psychedelic self-treatment for mental health conditions
pmc-11311900.creator: Claire Walker, Timothy Piatkowski, Jason Ferris, Emma Davies, Monica Barratt, Adam Winstock, Cheneal Puljević
pmc-11311900.description: Introduction:This study explores how individuals self-treat psychiatric conditions with psychedelics outside medical guidance bridging the gap in understanding unregulated therapeutic use.Aims:The primary objective was to extract specific factors underlying the effects of psychedelics, exploring their relationship with the need for medication, particularly for mental health conditions like depression and anxiety.

pmc-11374189.title: Urothelial cancer: state of art in Ukraine and improvement pathways
pmc-11374189.creator: Maksym Pikul, Prokip Gordiichuk, Eduard Stakhovsky
pmc-11374189.description: Aim:This study aims to assess the effectiveness of urothelial cancer treatment in Ukraine, utilizing population-based data from the National Cancer Registry. The primary goal is to evaluate trends and approaches to therapy, with a focus on overall survival rates in patients with urothelial tumors.

pmc-12385788.title: The Influence of Myofascial Techniques on the Range of Motion and Flat Foot Efficiency in Adults with Symptomatic Flat Foot: A Controlled Randomised Trial
pmc-12385788.creator: Sabina Kaczor, Urszula Żmudzińska, Aleksandra Kulis
pmc-12385788.description: Objective: Symptomatic flat foot is quite a common pathology in adults. Myofascial release is one of the physiotherapeutic methods that are currently very often used in the treatment of musculoskeletal diseases. This study aimed to assess the impact of myofascial release on the range of motion and functional efficiency of the flat foot in adults.

pmc-13062862.title: Real world outcomes of darolutamide activity and safety in treating hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
pmc-13062862.creator: Shuo Liang, Xuyu Zhang, Tong Lu, Zhigang Wu, Hongqian Guo, Junlong Zhuang
pmc-13062862.description: BackgroundDarolutamide is a next-generation androgen receptor (AR) inhibitor, used in the treatment of prostate cancer. There is currently limited real-world data available on its activity and safety. In our research, we collected real-world data to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of darolutamide in patients with castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

pmc-13092133.title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination on CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocyte profiles in an HIV-positive and HIV-negative female cohort
pmc-13092133.creator: Olive Khaliq, Niren Maharaj, Mikyle David, Ahmad Jassen, Nomakhuwa Tabane, Jagidesa Moodley
pmc-13092133.description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic led to rapid global vaccine deployment, especially among high-risk groups, such as individuals living with HIV. Data are limited, however, on the immunologic effects of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination—specifically, on CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocyte levels—in HIV-positive women in South Africa, a population with high HIV prevalence.

pmc-13232502.title: An increased number of heterozygous calls in the AxiomTM Equine Genotyping Array
pmc-13232502.creator: Annik Imogen Gmel, Ali Pirani, Liz McInnis, Markus Neuditschko
pmc-13232502.description: Single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays are commonly used in livestock genetics to investigate complex traits, including genome-wide associations and fine mapping, genomic prediction, and genetic diversity analyses. In a European equine diversity study, we analysed the Axiom Equine 670K SNP genotype data from 2,768 equids representing 20 horse breeds and one donkey breed.

pmc-13435581.title: Impaired NADH-linked mitochondrial respiration disrupts ventral midbrain neuronal programs in POLG disease
pmc-13435581.creator: Anbin Chen, Tsering Yangzom, Gareth John Sullivan, Kristina Xiao Liang

pmc-13522487.title: CD97/ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
pmc-13522487.creator: Gabriela Aust, Anna-Lena Hoh, Jehan Alladina, Neal P. Smith, Florian Höhna, Bingyu Wang, Christiane Kerner, Marita Wagner, Knut Krohn, Arkadiusz Pierzchalski, Nele Häussler, Alexandra Chloe Villani, Josalyn L. Cho, Benjamin D. Medoff, Ana C. Zenclussen, Matthias Steinert, Jörg Hamann, Marianne Quaas
pmc-13522487.description: Allergic asthma results from an uncontrolled type 2 immune response to inhaled allergens. Here, we investigate the function of CD97/ADGRE5, expressed in mouse and human immune and lung epithelial cells, in this disease. Female Cd97−/− mice exhibit an exacerbated asthmatic phenotype across multiple models, primarily due to CD97 loss on immune cells.

pmc-13543059.title: A Pan‐European Whole‐Microbiome Study of Wastewater Influent: Prokaryotes, Protists, Fungi, and Metazoa
pmc-13543059.creator: Niklas Nett, Kenneth Dumack
pmc-13543059.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microbial communities entering wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) through untreated sewage represent an important interface between human, environmental, and treatment‐associated microbiomes, yet our understanding of their biogeography remains poorly resolved, particularly for microbial eukaryotes. Using shotgun metagenomic time‐series data from influent samples of seven WWTPs across a European latitudinal gradient, we analyzed the taxonomic composition and dynamics of bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa.
